name: Step-down (eccentric)
summary: Standing on a step on one leg, lower the other heel slowly toward the floor and rise again.
setup: Stand on a step facing the phone, weight on the working leg, other foot hanging in front. Bend the standing knee to lower the free heel toward the floor, touch lightly, and press back up. Hips level throughout.
brief: Stand on a step, weight on the working leg, other foot hanging in front. Bend the standing knee to lower the free heel toward the floor, touch lightly, and press back up.
why: Facing the phone shows the standing knee angle for the count and, more usefully, the pelvis: the free-side hip dropping is the sign the outer hip muscles have let go.
regression: Lower step, fingertips on a wall.
contraindications: Kneecap pain on the way down.

faults.label: Hip dropping on the free side
faults.tip: Think of lifting the free hip as you lower. A dropping pelvis means the standing hip is not holding you.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Knee caving inward
faults.tip: Keep the standing knee over the middle of the foot as you lower.

faults.label: Dropping instead of lowering
faults.tip: The whole point is the slow lowering. If the heel lands with a thud, the step is too tall.

faults.label: Taking weight on the lower foot
faults.tip: The heel touches the floor and comes straight back. Weight stays on the top leg.

guide.surface: A stable step; a wall within fingertip reach.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain, or the knee collapsing inward.
guide.cannotSee: How far the knee travels forward over the toes.

points.t: Knee bends over the middle of the foot; heel stays down.
Both hip bones stay level as you lower.
